steps.content: [Scene Transition - Clementine's Study]

The room is quiet. Only the occasional rustle of turning pages and the scratch of pen on paper can be heard. Clementine sits across from you, a notebook of her own opened before her. Its pages are filled with a chaotic web of scribbled words and connecting lines.

Every so often, she pauses to think before adding another note, then draws a few more lines connecting different words. From a distance, the layers of lines and words begin to resemble a butterfly sketched in ink.
You try to make sense of her notes, but they're far too much of a mess. You study them for some time, until even Clementine can no longer ignore your staring and looks up.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: How are you coming along, Chief?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Almost there. I'm making good progress. I just need to rest my eyes for a moment.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Still need a bit more time, but I'm getting close. I just need to rest my eyes for a moment.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But you've been on the same page for nearly ten minutes now.
You look away, choosing silence over a response. Sensing your struggle, Clementine extends a helping hand once more.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Even the greatest detectives would hit a dead end every now and then. There's no shame in it.
She waves the draft paper in her hand.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Would you like a hint?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Oh? You're sure you don't need it?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You've been trying to sneak a peek for quite a while now... are you sureee you don't want a closer look?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Sure. Since you're offering, I'll take you up on it.
You take the draft paper from her, only to find that no matter which way you turn it, the writing is completely illegible. There's nothing but indecipherable scribbles here.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...Are you messing with me?

You slap the useless piece of paper back onto the table with visible annoyance. Seeing that her prank was successful, Clementine stands up with a satisfied smile and heads toward the bookshelf under the pretense of fetching fresh draft paper, leaving you space to think.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: No thanks. I can tell from that look on your face that you've set up another trap for me.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What a shame. I was hoping to play the role of a helpful assistant like W****n or H*******s—
Clementine stands up with an exaggerated sigh and heads toward the bookshelf under the pretense of fetching fresh draft paper, leaving you space to think.
[Special Portrait: Praeva Novel]
Your gaze returns to the pages. The detective in the story has finished searching the crime scene, but you, the reader, still can't piece together the clues to identify a concrete suspect.
Just then, a new approach comes to mind.
Unlike the version published online, this manuscript is hand-edited. That means it's most likely the original draft... So, while Clementine's away—
"The detective gathers everyone in the dining car. The truth is about to be revealed. He raises his hand, pointing toward the culprit—"
steps.female_content: "The detective gathers everyone in the dining car. The truth is about to be revealed. She raises her hand, pointing toward the culprit—"

steps.content: You flip to the next page. The pages that follow are completely blank. The story cuts off right before the big reveal.
Tucked into the last page of the manuscript is a note. A line of elegant handwriting graces the paper:
Dear naughty little cheater, Too bad. The final chapter hasn't been published yet. I'll only send out the manuscript for the last chapter after you leave.
You look up, realizing something. And sure enough, you're met with a mischievous smile.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Did I return at a bad time?

options: No, you came back at just the right time.

steps.content: This time, you're the one who sighs.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Games usually give new players beginner bonuses. Likewise, this first-time reader of mystery novels here needs a quick tutorial.
Clementine gives you a questioning look. You flip back through the manuscript, organizing the clues as you go.
[Background - Train Carriage, Filter #65 Dims]

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: The victim and the detective separated at around 10 o'clock and went to sleep in their respective rooms. Her door was locked from the inside, and there are no signs of tampering... So, if you rule out the detective as a suspect, the culprit could only have entered through the hidden door from the adjacent room 103.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Furthermore, the victim showed no signs of struggle. She most likely couldn't control her body when she was attacked, which suggests that she had taken some kind of sedative before going to sleep.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...The pocket watch on the victim was shattered by external force and is stopped at 1:05. There was a power outage at that time, which is the perfect opportunity to strike.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: There were many sounds in the corridor during the night of the crime... Everyone was particularly active around 1 o'clock, but their alibis can only be verified through testimonies. There's no physical evidence.
The scattered clues connect piece by piece, yet they fail to give you the answer. Just who is it that committed the murder? And how was it done?
[Back to Background - Clementine's Study]
You turn your gaze back to the architect of this whole conundrum.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't give me that look. This is a challenge—what fun would it be if the puzzle was too easy?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Besides... what you're missing is simply a bit of experience in a battle of wits with the author.
As Clementine speaks, she flips the page in your hand.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: See? I left you a hint from the very beginning, didn't I?
On the back of that message, there's actually another line of text—
If you find yourself stuck... Why not try approaching the problem from a different angle? You might discover something new.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That's... supposed to be a hint?
When the motive cannot be determined, what other method can you use to identify the true culprit?
Your hand, which was flipping through the pages, suddenly stops. Your eyes are drawn to a particular line of text.
Die! Die!!! Just wait, ▇▇▇. I will never forgive you! If you don't ▇▇▇, I'll bury everyone on this train with you!

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...Twelve stab wounds. If the intent was to kill, the first few would have been more than enough... So what was the point of the frenzied stabbing that followed? Revenge? Or... was it rage?

options: Who would harbor such deep hatred toward the victim?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: In other words... someone else on this train, aside from the victim, must be connected to the Redwood.

You look up, just in time to see Clementine picking up her pen to add another stroke to the indecipherable scribbles. As she meets your gaze, she narrows her eyes in a smile, almost like she wasn't the one who left that hint.
What is this woman plotting? And how is she connected to that fire?
[Battle 5, Train Scene]
